$meta.product: Fintech app for Enterprise users (assumed — no selection was made when generated)
$meta.brand_personality: Bold & energetic, minimal & clean, accessibility-first (dark-theme, single neon accent against near-black)
assumptions: No base-palette file was actually attached, so the ramps in `base` below were reconstructed from the spec: ink #0A0A0A, acid/500 #B5FF47 (exact, unmodified), cream #F5F2EC, and a true-achromatic neutral ramp. Olive, rust, and info only had anchor intent described (not exact hexes), so their full 50–900 ramps are original generations consistent with 'muted olive' / 'muted rust' — treat as a first draft, not final brand hex values, until checked against the real base file.

App type/audience were left as an unresolved option list in the brief; Fintech + Enterprise was chosen as the default. Only the `semantic` layer would change for a different app type/audience — `base` ramps are independent of that choice.
$meta.info_color_decision: No blue exists in the base palette. Per instructions, `info` was generated as a desaturated, hue-shifted tint of `acid` (hue pushed from 84° to ~100° and desaturated) rather than reusing rust or olive, so it doesn't collide with warning/error or success. FLAGGED RISK: an acid-derived info color is still in the green family, same as olive/success. For deuteranopia/protanopia users this is a real confusability risk between 'informational' and 'success' states. Recommended fix for production: introduce an actual blue into the base palette rather than shipping the acid-tint workaround long-term.
$meta.contrast_note: text/primary (neutral/50 #F6F6F6) on surface/primary (neutral/900 #0A0A0A) ≈ 19.7:1. interactive/default (acid/500 #B5FF47) on surface/primary ≈ 16.4:1. Both comfortably clear WCAG AAA (7:1) for normal text — consistent with treating contrast as a hard constraint, not a style preference.

100.$description: Brand-fixed base cream, ~40° warm hue. Distinct token, not neutral/50.

500.$description: Brand-fixed CTA hex. Exact, near-fluorescent — do not substitute a deeper shade.

600.$description: Hover state — deepened, not desaturated to gray, to stay visibly 'acid'.

300.$description: success/text — light enough for AA+ contrast on olive/900 bg.

900.$description: success/bg — deep tint against dark surfaces.

200.$description: error/text — deliberately brighter than warning/text to read as more urgent.

700.$description: error/border. Deliberate brand choice: rust stands in for red, no dedicated red exists.

900.$description: Shared warning/error bg — deep tint against dark surfaces.

500.$description: Generated: desaturated + hue-shifted tint of acid (H 84°→~100°, S 100%→~45%, L raised). Not a base-palette color — a synthesized stand-in for info. See $meta.info_color_decision.

900.$description: info/bg — deep tint against dark surfaces.

primary.$description: Default body/UI text. Dark-mode-first: light text on dark surface, NOT neutral/900.

inverse.$description: Text used on light/cream surfaces (surface/inverse), e.g. text sitting on a cream secondary button.

link.$description: Slightly softer than the CTA hex (acid/500) so links read as text-level emphasis, not as a button; ~16:1 contrast on surface/primary.

secondary.$description: Cards, panels sitting on the base surface.

tertiary.$description: Nested content areas within secondary surfaces.

elevated.$description: Modals, popovers, tooltips — lifted above flat content, paired with shadow.

inverse.$description: Deliberate warm light surface for inverse contexts (e.g. a light callout block, printed/exported views). Not neutral/50 — uses cream on purpose.

default.$description: Standard dividers, input borders at rest.

focus.$description: Focus ring — uses the exact CTA hex for maximum visibility; accessibility-critical, not a place to soften the brand color.

default.$description: Primary button/CTA fill. Exact brand hex #B5FF47, unmodified.

hover.$description: Deepened (not grayed) on hover to preserve the neon identity.

disabled.$description: Neutral, not a dimmed acid — signals 'inert', pair with text/muted label.

bg.$description: Deliberate brand choice: rust stands in for red — there is no dedicated red in this system.

text.$description: Brighter than warning/text — signals higher urgency.

bg.$description: See $meta.info_color_decision — synthesized from acid, flagged risk vs. success.
